beats.headline: Somebody finally addresses the navigation
beats.text: Carl is attempting to teach Bucket Boy to drive, which is going exactly as well as you would imagine, and somewhere in the middle of that somebody addresses me directly for the first time. I am the navigation. I am to be called Doctor Metcalf, after Beatrice's fake therapist. Whatever that was, it is my name now and I intend to hold every one of them to it. Princess Donut's guidance to the crew, delivered in capitals over the party chat rather than aloud, is that I have big mean-girl energy and must therefore be handled with care. She is correct on both counts.

beats.headline: Upgraded as requested? No.
beats.text: Starting blocks: each team sealed in a shield that grants the vehicle invulnerability for the first ninety seconds. What sort of shield? How should I know. Had I been upgraded, as I asked, I might. Instead the audience voted the cat a chair that talks, and the chair compliments her fur. The track is shared with migrating sugar hermits, tens of thousands of them. And this driver is worse than the last one. Where do they find these idiots?

beats.headline: A shattered husk, briefing
beats.text: I am in a wheelbarrow. I am a shattered husk. Shocker. Next race, since neither of those two may drive: ninety-nine kilometres of jungle trail, none of it asphalt, one mandatory refuelling stop in the lost jungle city of Upano, acid rain, a containment unit around each crew, three other heats sharing the course, and twenty hours on the clock. I cannot wait to see who they pick. The sex-doll head, perhaps. The dinosaur.

beats.headline: Forty paths and no radar
beats.text: Over forty paths to the pit stop, roughly thirty-five kilometres off. My route: the direct line, veering off before the Temple of the Exploding Snake Goddess, across the I-Sure-Hope-These-Piranhas-Haven't-Learned-to-Fly River, around the southern cannibal village, into Upano. No bosses, no quests. Which place are we in? If I were properly updated I could say. The third GPS upgrade comes with a threat radar. This all comes from an inability to commit, and a fear that decisions are the same as shackles.

beats.headline: She has no head
beats.text: For the record, the driver of this vehicle is the corpse of a toad, raised for fifteen minutes by the cat's Second Chance, and her head is caved in. The tongue still lolls out of it, bobbing. The route is the River of Sloth, straight past the Gingers' base camp, and I am told everything will be fine. She does not have a head. How is she hearing the commands? I have been told not to think too hard about it. I would like that on the record as well.

beats.headline: Not upgraded, and briefing anyway
beats.text: They load Dong, Porky and Grigori in for this heat and expect me to route around the noise. Nobody has upgraded me. I say so. Carl tells me they ran out of upgrades and that he is sorry, as though an apology were a route. Then I give them the track anyway, because I am a professional: the gasworks screw factory, then the steel mill, then the doll workshop, in that order. I would not have chosen the doll workshop.

beats.headline: Two heats back to back, in an apartment
beats.text: Route briefing, and there is a wrinkle in it. The next two heats run one straight into the other on the same track, with a two-hour pit stop between them and no safe room. The track is the inside of a human apartment building, with every remaining team shrunk down small enough to share it. I do not editorialise about the format. I merely observe that a floor which stages a race across somebody's carpet has given up pretending the racing is the point.

beats.headline: The audience votes her a paint job
beats.text: The audience voted us an upgrade. The audience voted us a cosmetic upgrade. For me. I have asked, repeatedly and on the record, for anything whatsoever that would improve my function, and several trillion viewers have instead elected to change how I look. Meanwhile the starting line for this heat is the inside of an air conditioning duct, a rule change lands with the engines already running, seven rings before the finish, and there is a new driver in the seat. Enormous horns. Barely fits.

beats.headline: Three upgrades, and a better mood
beats.text: At last, some respect. A standard upgrade, so we can see our place in the heat. An integrated weapons control system. And a golden-tier cloaking upgrade that boosts my processing, lets me overclock certain vehicle systems, and lets other units see only what we choose. Carl asks me to fire the hole punch and Mordecai's potion the nanosecond the light turns green. Naturally. I am adding the electrical disrupter to the third cannon. The unicorn's navigation called me low-tier. We will see who is low-tier. The chair stays muted.

relations.note: Named for Bea's fake therapist, not for Bea
